rules.title: Annual allowable rent increase for March 2026–February 2027
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, landlords must use an annual allowable increase of 1.6% of the tenant's base rent for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.exemptions: Limited to rent-controlled units; the announcement does not define which units are rent-controlled.
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board, Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced, January 14, 2026
rules.quoted_span:
For
rent-controlled units
, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
To calculate the dollar amount of the 1.6% annual rent increase, multiply the tenant's base rent by .016. For example, if the tenant's base rent is $2,000.00, the annual increase would be calculated as follows: $2,000.00 x .016 = $32.00. The tenant's new base rent would be $2,032.00 ($2,000.00 + $32.00).

rules.title: Just cause must be the dominant eviction motive
rules.requirement: A landlord evicting a tenant covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions must have one of the 17 specified just-cause reasons as the dominant motive; mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not suffice. A landlord who unlawfully evicts or attempts to evict a tenant may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental tenancies covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions. Coverage includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency, even when exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limitations. The source does not fully define covered rental tenancies, enumerate eviction exemptions, or identify which tenancies regulated by another government agency are included; those address-level eligibility questions require review.
rules.exemptions: The summarized grounds are: nonpayment, habitual late payment, or frequent bounced checks; failure to cure a substantial lease breach; nuisance or substantial interference with the landlord's or other tenants' comfort, safety, or enjoyment that is severe, continuing, or reoccurring; illegal use, excluding mere occupancy of an unwarranted unit and a single Chapter 41A short-term rental violation cured within 30 days of the landlord's written notice; refusal after written request to renew an expired agreement for a like term on materially the same terms; refusal after written notice to cease to permit legally required landlord access; an unapproved subtenant being the only tenant remaining at the agreement's end, with approval potentially oral or implied by the landlord's conduct; owner occupancy or, in limited circumstances, occupancy by immediate family; good-faith recovery to sell pursuant to an approved condominium conversion; demolition or permanent removal of an individual unit from housing use; capital improvements or rehabilitation temporarily making the unit uninhabitable, with immediate reoccupancy after completion; substantial rehabilitation of an essentially uninhabitable building at least 50 years old, with proposed work costing at least 75% of new construction; withdrawal of all building rental units under the Ellis Act; lead remediation or abatement required by Health Code Articles 11 or 26; demolition or permanent removal pursuant to a City development agreement under Administrative Code Chapter 56; expiration of a Good Samaritan occupancy agreement with eviction notice served within 60 days after expiration, where the tenancy provides a reduced-rent temporary replacement unit to a tenant displaced by emergency or disaster; and completion of a development project requiring demolition under Planning Code Section 317. The source does not detail the limited circumstances permitting immediate-family occupancy or all requirements of the referenced grounds. Exemption from rent increase limitations does not itself establish exemption from eviction protections.

rules.title: Just cause for removal of housing services
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a just-cause reason to take away or remove access to covered housing services, including garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms. A landlord complying with Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove certain services, including parking and storage, to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work required by the Building Code.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies within the source's discussion of rental tenancies covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions. Those protections can include newly constructed units first receiving a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for Costa-Hawkins rent increases, and some tenancies with rent regulated by another government agency despite exemption from rent increase limits. The source does not fully specify tenancy coverage or exemptions, identify the included government-regulated tenancies, or establish whether the housing-services provision has any additional address-level limitations. These eligibility questions require review.
rules.exemptions: The service list is nonexclusive. Temporary removal of certain housing services for mandatory Building Code soft-story seismic retrofit work is permitted only when the landlord has complied with Ordinance Section 37.2(r); the source does not reproduce those requirements or fully identify the services eligible for this exception.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord also needs a "just cause“ reason to take away or remove access to certain
housing services
, including but not limited to garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms. However, a landlord who has complied with the requirements of Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may
temporarily remove certain housing services
, including parking and storage spaces, in order to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work required by
the Building Code
.
Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance. This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies that are eligible for a rent increase under the
Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act,
and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.

rules.title: Immediate reoccupancy after temporary displacement for work
rules.requirement: When a landlord recovers possession for capital improvements or rehabilitation work that makes a covered rental unit temporarily uninhabitable, the landlord must allow the tenant to reoccupy the unit immediately after the work is completed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental tenancies covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions. The source includes newly constructed units first receiving a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for Costa-Hawkins rent increases, and some tenancies with rent regulated by another government agency despite exemption from rent increase limits. It does not fully define tenancy coverage, enumerate eviction exemptions, or identify the included government-regulated tenancies; those address-level eligibility questions require review.
rules.exemptions: This reoccupancy duty is stated for capital improvements or rehabilitation that temporarily makes the unit uninhabitable. The source separately lists substantial rehabilitation of an essentially uninhabitable building at least 50 years old with proposed work costing at least 75% of new construction; it does not expressly extend this reoccupancy duty to that separate ground or to permanent removal from housing use.
